item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00217","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C13","C11","C05"],"selected_candidate_label":"C13","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C13 supplies essentially the complete two-part drafting template for the child: designation of a single named agency whose functions have a direct and immediate connection with national defense under section 103(a), followed by application of Title I to that agency's contracts and related subcontracts under section 102 from a specified effective date. The child principally substitutes the Bureau of Reclamation and a new date. C11 and C05 use the same machinery and much of the same language, but their plural, multi-agency formulations are a slightly less exact fit than C13's single-agency form.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The Bureau of Reclamation, which exercises functions having direct and immediate connection with the national defense, is hereby designated, pursuant to section 103 (a) of the Act, as an agency of the Government included within the definition of the term \"Department\" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.","parent_excerpt":"The Bonneville Power Administration, which exercises functions having a direct and immediate connection with the national defense, is hereby designated, pursuant to subsection (a) of section 103 of the Act, as an agency coming within the definition of the term \"Department\" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.","explanation":"This is a distinctive, nearly verbatim single-agency designation provision, with only the agency name and minor wording/order changed."},{"child_excerpt":"In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act shall be applicable to all contracts with the Bureau of Reclamation, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued on or after the first day of July, 1952, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.","parent_excerpt":"In accordance with section 102 of the Act, the provisions of Title I of the Act shall be applicable to all contracts with the Bonneville Power Administration, and related subcontracts, to the extent of the amounts received or accrued on or after the first day of November, 1951, whether such contracts or subcontracts were made on, before, or after that date.","explanation":"The second operative provision is virtually identical and preserves the same statutory trigger, covered contracts and subcontracts, accrual rule, and retroactive coverage formula while changing only the agency and effective date."}]}
